decisions.reason: Glass-silicon wafers with through contacts are a core extension of the firm's structured packaging-wafer competence, and the semiconductor boom of 2021-2022 lifted performance above aspiration, so there is no shortfall to trigger search for other uses of these resources.

Carrier wafers for smaller diameters cost little to keep within the established production and fit the stated direction toward reusable carriers, so the slack from strong semiconductor demand allows the firm to retain them.
The Cu-interposer is a flagship that builds on the firm's own R&D and advanced packaging trends, so with performance at or above aspiration management will keep backing it while its market develops.
The Wafer Universe off-the-shelf brand is a low-risk flagship channel close to the core business that benefits from high wafer demand, so there is no reason to drop it.

Glass-based circuit boards are distant from the core offer and their results are more uncertain, but organisational slack during the semiconductor upswing likely lets the firm carry them a while longer, even though they are the most likely candidate to be dropped.
